newsitem.title: India: Indian shares add gains, firm outlook.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares add gains, firm outlook.

text.p: Indian bourses rallied for the second straight day on Wednesday as fresh buying by market participants fuelled the rise in share prices, traders said.
They said fewer sellers and buying by FIIs and local operators triggered the sharp rise.
"There was supply mismatch," said a trader. "There were more buyers at (BSE index of) 3,300 than when it was 3,000."
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) soared 114.73 points or 3.56 percent to end at 3,341.86, tad below the day's highest mark of 3,344.35.
Wednesday's rally followed a 96.92-point rise on Tuesday sparked by a freer credit policy announced by the central bank at the long weekend which set off cuts in lending rates by banks.
The 50-share National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 32.20 points or 3.5 percent to 951.29 and the CRISIL-500 index rose 19.37 points or 3.14 percent to 636.65.
However, analysts said they expected the market to cool towards the week's close when profit-takers get active.
"I don't see the rally ... sustaining for very long," Vikas Saraf, research head at SSKI Securities, told Reuters.
"None of the major indications on the economic front have changed. We still see a lot of question marks around," said Sanjay Agarwal, chief executive of Lloyds Securities.
"The outlook is cautious. The 3,350 mark is a level where we have to wait and watch to see if the rally sustains," he said.

Top stocks TISCO rallied 17.50 rupees to 192.75, SBI 11.25 to 240, Bajaj Auto 25.0 to 996.50, ACC 95.75 to 1,645.75, ITC 11.75 to 322.50, TELCO 12.50 to 442.25, Indian Hotel 22.25 to 653.50, Hind Lever 10.50 to 825 and Reliance 8.0 to 214.75.
